blue_green.title: Pigment Blue 15:3 & Pigment Green 7: The Separate Transition Date Explained
blue_green.subtitle: Why these two specific pigments had their own timeline and what their legal status is across the European Union today.
blue_green.date_highlight_body: Under Commission Regulation (EU) 2020/2081, Pigment Blue 15:3 (CI 74160) and Pigment Green 7 (CI 74260) were granted a derogation deferring restriction until 4 January 2023. That derogation has expired. Today, both pigments are fully restricted under Entry 75.
blue_green.pb15_desc: Copper phthalocyanine blue (alpha form). Widely used for decades to achieve bright cyan and blue hues. Prohibited under Entry 75 due to classification in Annex II of the Cosmetic Products Regulation (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009). The derogation expired 4 January 2023.
blue_green.pg7_desc: Polychlorinated copper phthalocyanine. The standard industrial pigment for rich, stable green tones. Prohibited under Entry 75 via the same cosmetic Annex II mechanism. Derogation expired 4 January 2023.
blue_green.status_today_heading: What this means for studios today
blue_green.status_today_item1: Inks containing Pigment Blue 15:3 or Pigment Green 7 placed on the market or used in the EU after 4 January 2023 do not meet REACH Annex XVII Entry 75.
blue_green.status_today_item2: Manufacturers must formulate blue and green tones using alternative approved colorants or provide documented exemption proof under relevant member state law.
blue_green.source_reference: Legal Source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 of 14 December 2020, Paragraph 4(c) of Entry 75, amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH).

maker_questions.title: What to Ask the Ink Maker: Printable Question Sheet
maker_questions.subtitle: There is no such thing as an official 'compliance certificate' under EU law. Compliance is proven by manufacturer technical dossiers, SDS sheets, and accredited laboratory testing. Print or export this questionnaire for your suppliers.
maker_questions.sheet_doc_desc: Standard studio inquiry questionnaire for ink manufacturers and distributors.
maker_questions.checklist_heading: Mandatory Questions per EU Regulation 2020/2081 Entry 75
maker_questions.q1_desc: Has the manufacturer issued a written declaration specifying that this exact batch formulation complies with REACH Annex XVII Entry 75?
maker_questions.q2_desc: Does the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) Section 3 state all constituent substances with exact CAS and CI numbers, including any pigments present above 0.1% by weight?
maker_questions.q3_desc: Can the manufacturer provide independent laboratory test results certifying that impurities are within the legal thresholds (e.g., Lead ≤ 0.7 mg/kg, Arsenic ≤ 0.5 mg/kg, Cadmium ≤ 0.5 mg/kg, Nickel ≤ 5 mg/kg, Mercury ≤ 0.5 mg/kg)?
maker_questions.q4_desc: Are test results available verifying that primary aromatic amines listed in Appendix 13 (such as o-anisidine, 4-aminobiphenyl) do not exceed 5 mg/kg individually?
maker_questions.q5_title: 5. Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) in Black Formulations
maker_questions.q5_desc: If the formulation contains Carbon Black (CI 77266), does the batch analysis confirm benzo[a]pyrene ≤ 5 µg/kg (5 ppb) and total PAHs ≤ 0.5 mg/kg?
maker_questions.q6_desc: Does the bottle physically carry: (a) 'Mixture for use in tattoos or permanent make-up', (b) unique batch reference number, (c) complete ingredient list, (d) nickel/chromium safety warnings if applicable, (e) expiry or period-after-opening indicator?

plain_language_panel.title: What REACH Annex XVII Entry 75 Actually Requires
plain_language_panel.subtitle: Commission Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 establishes legal restrictions on chemical substances in tattoo inks and permanent make-up across the European Union. Here is how the rule works for artists, piercers, and studio owners in plain terms.
plain_language_panel.section1_lead: Responsibility is shared across the supply chain, but the artist has direct legal exposure upon application.
plain_language_panel.section1_maker_title: The Supplier / Importer Placing on the Market:
plain_language_panel.section1_maker_desc: Under REACH Article 67 and Entry 75, manufacturers and EU importers are legally prohibited from placing non-compliant mixtures on the market. They are responsible for formulating within concentration limits, screening for impurities, providing an accurate Safety Data Sheet (SDS) compliant with REACH Annex II, and correctly labelling containers.
plain_language_panel.section1_artist_desc: Under paragraph 1 of Entry 75, tattoo artists are prohibited from using any mixture for tattooing purposes that does not comply with the regulation. An artist cannot shift liability by stating 'the maker claimed it was compliant'. Studios must verify that labels carry required statements, check batch documentation, and ensure banned pigments are never applied to clients.
plain_language_panel.section2_title: 2. What a Bottle Label Must Physically Say
plain_language_panel.section2_lead: Under paragraph 4 of Entry 75, ink containers must visibly display these mandatory elements:
plain_language_panel.section2_item1: 'Mixture for use in tattoos or permanent make-up' explicitly on the packaging.
plain_language_panel.section2_item2: A unique batch reference number (LOT number) enabling complete supply chain traceability.
plain_language_panel.section2_item3: A full list of ingredients in descending order of weight or volume at formulation.
plain_language_panel.section2_item4: 'Contains nickel. Can cause allergic reactions.' if nickel exceeds 0.0005% (5 mg/kg).
plain_language_panel.section2_item5: 'Contains chromium (VI). Can cause allergic reactions.' if chromium (VI) exceeds 0.00005% (0.5 mg/kg).
plain_language_panel.section2_item6: Safety instructions for use, plus expiration or period-after-opening (PAO) indicators.
plain_language_panel.section3_title: 3. What SDS Section 3 Is (and Why It Might Not List Everything)
plain_language_panel.section3_lead: Safety Data Sheet Section 3 covers 'Composition / Information on Ingredients'.
plain_language_panel.section3_desc1: Under REACH Annex II, manufacturers are only legally required to disclose substances in Section 3 that are classified as hazardous under CLP (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008) and that exceed specific classification cut-off thresholds (typically 0.1% or 1% w/w).
plain_language_panel.section3_desc2: Non-hazardous carrier fluids (such as water or pharmaceutical glycerin) or ingredients below classification cut-offs may not appear in Section 3, even though the bottle label must list ingredients in descending order. Therefore, studios must evaluate both the bottle label and the SDS.
plain_language_panel.section4_title: 4. Prohibited vs Restricted vs Not Covered
plain_language_panel.section4_prohibited_desc: Substances listed in Annex II of the EU Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, substances in Annex IV with specific condition columns (not to be used in eye products, mucous membranes, or rinse-off only), and substances classified under CLP as Carcinogenic, Mutagenic, or Toxic for Reproduction (CMR) Cat 1A/1B/2, Skin Sensitisers, or Skin Corrosives without an Appendix 13 derogation. These must not be intentionally added or present above trace limits.
plain_language_panel.section4_restricted_desc: Substances listed in Table 13 (Appendix 13) of REACH Annex XVII with strict numerical concentration limits. For example: Lead (≤ 0.7 mg/kg), Arsenic (≤ 0.5 mg/kg), Nickel (≤ 5 mg/kg), and Carbon Black (total PAHs ≤ 0.5 mg/kg; benzo[a]pyrene ≤ 5 ppb). Formulations are permissible only when analytical testing proves impurities remain at or below these thresholds.
plain_language_panel.section4_not_covered_desc: Substances that carry no hazardous classification under CLP and are not listed in cosmetics annexes or Appendix 13 (e.g. pure Hamamelis Virginiana extract, distilled water, high-purity glycerin).
plain_language_panel.section5_title: 5. Why 'REACH Compliant' on a Bottle Is Not a Guarantee
plain_language_panel.section5_lead: The term 'REACH Compliant' is not a government seal or legal certificate.
plain_language_panel.section5_desc1: Any manufacturer can print 'REACH Compliant' on a label. European chemical enforcement authorities (such as ECHA and national market surveillance inspectors) evaluate analytical lab test results, batch purity, and complete SDS declarations—not marketing claims.
plain_language_panel.section5_desc2: To protect clients and demonstrate due diligence, studios should maintain a verification folder containing: (1) SDS with verified CAS/CI numbers, (2) Certificate of Analysis (COA) test reports for heavy metals and PAHs for each batch, and (3) client procedure logs linking bottle LOT numbers to client consent records.

nickel.description: Skin sensitiser 1 and Carcinogen 2. Maximum permitted soluble/total impurity ceiling is 5.0 mg/kg (ppm).

chromium_vi.description: Carcinogenic 1A, Mutagenic 1B, Skin Sensitiser 1. Maximum threshold is 0.5 mg/kg (ppm).

barium.description: Soluble barium impurity ceiling is 500 mg/kg (ppm).

zinc.description: Soluble zinc impurity ceiling is 2000 mg/kg (ppm).

cobalt.description: Carcinogenic 1B, Repr. 1B, Skin Sens. 1. Maximum threshold 0.5 mg/kg (ppm).

bap.description: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly in unrefined carbon black. Carcinogenic 1B. Threshold is 0.005 mg/kg (5 µg/kg or 5 ppb).

pahs_total.description: Sum of 8 REACH carcinogenic PAHs (Chrysene, Benz[a]anthracene, etc.). Maximum sum ceiling is 0.5 mg/kg (ppm).

pigment_red_170.entry_reference: Not listed in Entry 75 or Appendix 13
pigment_red_170.notes: High performance naphthol red. Widely used compliant red colorant in EU tattoo inks.

pigment_red_254.name: Pigment Red 254
pigment_red_254.entry_reference: Not listed in Entry 75 or Appendix 13
pigment_red_254.notes: Diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) red pigment. Major compliant red pigment in REACH-compliant inks.

pigment_red_101.name: Pigment Red 101
pigment_red_101.exact_limit: Appendix 13 trace metal impurity thresholds apply (Ni ≤ 5 mg/kg, Pb ≤ 0.7 mg/kg, As ≤ 0.5 mg/kg)
pigment_red_101.notes: Inorganic synthetic iron oxide red. Permitted provided heavy metal impurities comply with Appendix 13 limits.

pigment_yellow_14.name: Pigment Yellow 14
pigment_yellow_14.notes: Disazo diarylide yellow pigment. Prohibited due to hazardous cleavage into 3,3-dichlorobenzidine.

pigment_yellow_83.name: Pigment Yellow 83
pigment_yellow_83.notes: Diarylide yellow pigment prohibited in tattoo inks due to amine cleavage risks.

pigment_yellow_138.name: Pigment Yellow 138
pigment_yellow_138.entry_reference: Not listed in Entry 75 or Appendix 13
pigment_yellow_138.notes: Quinophthalone yellow colorant. Permitted and widely used in REACH-compliant yellow and green inks.

ethanol.name: Ethanol / Ethyl Alcohol
ethanol.entry_reference: Not listed in Entry 75 or Appendix 13
ethanol.notes: Common carrier solvent and antimicrobial diluent. Not restricted under Entry 75.

benzyl_alcohol.name: Benzyl Alcohol
benzyl_alcohol.entry_reference: Entry 75, paragraph 1(a); Annex V, entry 34 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009
benzyl_alcohol.notes: Cosmetic preservative and solvent. Concentration limit: 1.0% by weight.

phenoxyethanol.name: Phenoxyethanol
phenoxyethanol.entry_reference: Entry 75, paragraph 1(a); Annex V, entry 29 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009
phenoxyethanol.notes: Cosmetic preservative. Maximum permitted concentration: 1.0% by weight.

polyethylene_glycol.name: Polyethylene Glycol (PEG)
polyethylene_glycol.entry_reference: Not listed in Entry 75 or Appendix 13
polyethylene_glycol.notes: Humectant, viscosity modifier, and dispersion aid. Not restricted under Entry 75.

benzoic_acid.name: Benzoic Acid / Sodium Benzoate
benzoic_acid.entry_reference: Entry 75, paragraph 1(a); Annex V, entry 1 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009
benzoic_acid.notes: Preservative. Maximum concentration 0.5% by weight as benzoic acid.

rosin_colophonium.name: Rosin / Colophonium
rosin_colophonium.notes: Pine resin derivative. Skin sensitiser (Cat. 1B). Restricted to 0.001% by weight (10 mg/kg) under Entry 75.

o_anisidine.name: o-Anisidine
o_anisidine.notes: Primary aromatic amine (Carcinogen 1B). Appendix 13 concentration limit: 5 mg/kg.

benzidine.name: Benzidine
benzidine.notes: Potent human carcinogen (Carcinogen 1A). Appendix 13 concentration limit: 5 mg/kg.

dichlorobenzidine.name: 3,3'-Dichlorobenzidine
dichlorobenzidine.notes: Carcinogenic aromatic amine (Carcinogen 1B). Cleavage product of diarylide yellow and orange pigments. Appendix 13 threshold: 5 mg/kg.

chloroaniline.name: 4-Chloroaniline
chloroaniline.notes: Aromatic amine (Carcinogen 1B). Appendix 13 concentration threshold: 5 mg/kg.

eval.eu_compliant_desc: Permitted for tattoo & PMU formulation within REACH Annex XVII Entry 75 concentration limits.
eval.eu_compliant_action: Verify SDS Section 3 and retain batch record on client file for 5 years.
eval.eu_bluegreen_desc: CI 74160 and CI 74260 derogation period expired on 4 January 2023. Prohibited above 0.1% w/w in EU.
eval.eu_bluegreen_action: Do not inject within EU territory. Switch to compliant alternative formulations.
eval.eu_banned_desc: Strictly prohibited in mixtures for tattooing under Annex XVII Entry 75 or SVHC Candidate List.
eval.eu_banned_action: Quarantine bottle immediately and notify studio supplier.
eval.eu_restricted_desc: Subject to explicit statutory concentration limit in Appendix 13 table.
eval.eu_restricted_action: Check Certificate of Analysis (COA) to ensure concentration is below statutory ppm threshold.
eval.us_standard_desc: Regulated under FD&C Act and MoCRA. Subject to mandatory facility registration and product listing.
eval.us_standard_action: Record bottle lot number in client file and retain for at least 3 years for adverse event traceability.
eval.us_color_paradox_desc: Color additive under FD&C Act without FDA injection approval. Permitted via enforcement discretion under MoCRA.
eval.us_color_paradox_action: Ensure manufacturer has completed MoCRA cosmetic product listing and safety substantiation.
eval.us_metal_desc: FDA CFSAN monitors heavy metal impurities and issues safety alerts for adulterated batches.
eval.us_metal_action: Verify manufacturer purity documentation and check FDA recall database before application.
eval.au_listed_desc: Introduction regulated by AICIS. Chemical substance is listed on Australian Inventory of Industrial Chemicals (AIIC).
eval.au_listed_action: Log bottle batch number in state-mandated skin penetration client register.
eval.au_metal_desc: Heavy metal toxicity evaluated under AICIS risk framework; state public health acts prohibit unsafe materials.
eval.au_metal_action: Ensure importer has submitted AICIS introduction categorisation and keep COA on site.
eval.au_banned_desc: Substance prohibited or restricted under AICIS hazardous chemical introduction standards.
eval.au_banned_action: Do not use in skin penetration procedures. Segregate stock.
eval.asean_standard_desc: Intradermal tattoo inks are not harmonized under ASEAN Cosmetic Directive (ACD). Regulated by national health acts.
eval.asean_standard_action: Comply with municipal studio licensing and national import documentation rules.
eval.asean_metal_desc: ACD Annex limits apply to topical cosmetics; national public health bodies inspect intradermal purity.
eval.asean_metal_action: Request international purity certificate matching EU or US quality benchmarks.
eval.asean_banned_desc: Substance listed in ACD Annex II (prohibited cosmetic ingredients) or national poison schedules.
eval.asean_banned_action: Prohibited for cosmetic and aesthetic procedures across member state jurisdictions.

jurisdictions.divergence_overview_desc: Tattoo and permanent make-up (PMU) ink regulation differs fundamentally across world regions. The European Union operates under precise statutory chemical limits, whereas the United States, Australia, and Southeast Asia govern inks through facility listings, industrial inventories, or national public health standards.

divergence.eu_statutory_summary: Dedicated chemical restriction under REACH Annex XVII Entry 75.
divergence.eu_statutory_specifics: Tattoo mixtures are defined as a distinct category under EU chemical law, binding all 27 EU member states plus EEA countries.
divergence.us_statutory_summary: Cosmetics under FD&C Act and MoCRA (2022).
divergence.us_statutory_specifics: Inks are legally classified as cosmetics; pigments are legally color additives subject to Section 721 of the FD&C Act.
divergence.au_statutory_summary: Industrial chemicals (federal) and skin penetration standards (state).
divergence.au_statutory_specifics: Federal AICIS scheme controls chemical importation and manufacture; state public health legislation governs studio practice.
divergence.asean_statutory_summary: Topical cosmetics (ACD) with non-harmonized intradermal inks.
divergence.asean_statutory_specifics: The ASEAN Cosmetic Directive governs topical preparations only; intradermal tattoo inks fall under municipal and national public health acts.
divergence.eu_thresholds_summary: Exact statutory ppm limits codified in Appendix 13.
divergence.eu_thresholds_specifics: Enforces 0.00005% (0.5 mg/kg) for carcinogens/mutagens, 0.1% general limit, and specific limits for 19 heavy metals.
divergence.us_thresholds_summary: No statutory ppm table; focus on adulteration and misbranding.
divergence.us_thresholds_specifics: Sections 601 and 602 prohibit poisonous or deleterious substances, but federal law contains no numeric ppm table for tattoo pigments.
divergence.au_thresholds_summary: No statutory ppm table under AICIS for tattoo inks.
divergence.au_thresholds_specifics: AICIS evaluates introductions based on human health risk bands rather than static finished-mixture ppm schedules.
divergence.asean_thresholds_summary: No regional ppm limits for intradermal tattoo formulations.
divergence.asean_thresholds_specifics: ACD Annexes establish ppm limits for topical cosmetics (e.g. Lead 20 ppm, Arsenic 5 ppm) which do not legally bind tattoo inks.
divergence.pigments_title: Pigment Approvals & The US Color Additive Paradox
divergence.eu_pigments_summary: Appendix 13 bans thousands of substances and specific CI colorants.
divergence.eu_pigments_specifics: Bans azo dyes cleaving to carcinogenic aromatic amines and colorants in Cosmetics Regulation Annex II and Annex IV with conditions.
divergence.us_pigments_summary: The Color Additive Paradox: unapproved yet sold under MoCRA.
divergence.us_pigments_specifics: No color additive has been approved by FDA for intradermal injection. Inks circulate legally under historical enforcement discretion.
divergence.au_pigments_specifics: Pigments must be listed on AIIC or introduced under an approved AICIS category. No specific tattoo positive list exists.
divergence.asean_pigments_summary: National import clearance and custom schedules.
divergence.asean_pigments_specifics: No unified ASEAN positive list for tattoo colorants; studios commonly rely on imported EU or US certified lines.
divergence.eu_metals_summary: 19 heavy metals and impurities with strict statutory ppm caps.
divergence.eu_metals_specifics: Appendix 13 specifies exact maximum limits, including Lead 0.7 mg/kg, Arsenic 0.5 mg/kg, Cadmium 0.5 mg/kg, and Mercury 0.5 mg/kg.
divergence.us_metals_summary: FDA safety alerts and microbial recall monitoring.
divergence.us_metals_specifics: FDA issues safety advisories and recalls when contaminated or adulterated inks cause non-tuberculous mycobacterial infections.
divergence.au_metals_summary: Chemical risk assessment and public health general safety duties.
divergence.au_metals_specifics: State health departments inspect studio hygiene and can seize contaminated product under broad public health powers.
divergence.asean_metals_summary: Topical cosmetic purity references used voluntarily.
divergence.asean_metals_specifics: Regional authorities may reference ACD topical metal limits as investigative guidelines during health complaints.
divergence.eu_facility_summary: CLP classification, SDS under Annex II, full INCI labeling.
divergence.eu_facility_specifics: Bottles must state 'Mixture for use in tattoos or permanent make-up', lot number, and full ingredients descending by weight.
divergence.us_facility_summary: Mandatory MoCRA facility registration and product listing.
divergence.us_facility_specifics: Facilities must register with FDA, list cosmetic products annually, maintain safety substantiation, and report serious adverse events.
divergence.au_facility_summary: AICIS business registration and annual declaration.
divergence.au_facility_specifics: Importers must hold active AICIS registration, submit annual chemical declarations, and keep categorisation records for 5 years.
divergence.asean_facility_summary: National company registration and import declarations.
divergence.asean_facility_specifics: Importers register with local commercial and health authorities (e.g. Singapore HSA, Thailand FDA, Indonesia BPOM).
divergence.eu_records_summary: Verification of REACH label statement and batch logging.
divergence.eu_records_specifics: Studio must ensure ink bottle bears mandatory statement and retain client batch traceability under national health decrees.
divergence.us_records_summary: 3-year lot number retention recommended for adverse events.
divergence.us_records_specifics: Under MoCRA, studios should document ink brand and lot number on client consent records for at least 3 years.
divergence.au_records_specifics: State legislation requires keeping client procedure records, sterilisation logs, and pigment batch numbers for local council health audits.
divergence.asean_records_summary: Municipal salon registers and client consent logs.
divergence.asean_records_specifics: Studios keep client consent forms, procedural notes, and supplier invoices according to local municipal ordinances.
divergence.eu_pmu_summary: Identical chemical limits apply to PMU and body tattoo inks.
divergence.eu_pmu_specifics: Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 covers all intradermal coloring mixtures identically, including microblading and cosmetic tattooing.
divergence.us_pmu_specifics: PMU pigments are subject to cosmetic product listing, adverse event reporting, and professional use labeling rules.
divergence.au_pmu_summary: Skin penetration and personal appearance services licensing.
divergence.au_pmu_specifics: PMU technicians must hold accredited infection control units under state public health regulations.
divergence.asean_pmu_summary: Aesthetic salon guidelines and ACD topical prep compliance.
divergence.asean_pmu_specifics: PMU salons must comply with local beauty council rules and ensure topical numbing agents meet national drug regulations.

jurisdictions.checklist_subheading: Key operational steps required to maintain verified records in each regulatory jurisdiction
jurisdictions.checklist_eu_item_1: Verify bottle states 'Mixture for use in tattoos or permanent make-up' and displays lot number.
jurisdictions.checklist_eu_item_2: Obtain and archive manufacturer Safety Data Sheet (SDS) with Annex II composition.
jurisdictions.checklist_eu_item_3: Log bottle batch number and client procedure date in studio record.
jurisdictions.checklist_us_item_1: Confirm manufacturer has completed MoCRA facility registration and cosmetic product listing.
jurisdictions.checklist_us_item_2: Record ink brand, shade name, and batch lot number on client consent documentation.
jurisdictions.checklist_us_item_3: Retain client procedure records for at least 3 years and establish adverse event reporting SOP.
jurisdictions.checklist_au_item_1: Verify ink chemicals are listed on AIIC or imported by an AICIS registered business.
jurisdictions.checklist_au_item_2: Record client details, date, and pigment batch number in skin penetration logbook.
jurisdictions.checklist_au_item_3: Maintain infection control qualification records for all operating artists.
jurisdictions.checklist_asean_item_1: Maintain supplier commercial invoices and import declaration paperwork on file.
jurisdictions.checklist_asean_item_2: Ensure all topical prep solutions, cleansers, and aftercare comply with ACD standards.
jurisdictions.checklist_asean_item_3: Maintain client signed consent forms and municipal health inspection certificates.
